possible_conditions.name: Common cold
possible_conditions.why_considered: Mild upper respiratory symptoms (sore throat, cough, nasal congestion) are characteristic of viral rhinitis.
possible_conditions.differentiating_factors: Typically gradual onset, mild or absent fever, absence of severe muscle aches or dyspnea.

possible_conditions.name: Influenza
possible_conditions.why_considered: Acute onset of systemic symptoms including fever, fatigue, cough, and myalgias aligns with influenza infection.
possible_conditions.differentiating_factors: Abrupt onset, higher fever, pronounced prostration and muscle pain compared to common cold.

possible_conditions.name: Other respiratory infection (e.g. Acute Bronchitis or Pharyngitis)
possible_conditions.why_considered: The reported symptoms can occur with several bacterial or viral respiratory tract infections.
possible_conditions.differentiating_factors: Persistent productive cough, localized tonsillar exudates, or prolonged duration.

possible_conditions.name: Allergic Rhinitis
possible_conditions.why_considered: Repetitive paroxysmal sneezing, clear rhinorrhea, and scratchy throat without marked fever indicate allergic sensitization.
possible_conditions.differentiating_factors: Itchy eyes/palate, seasonal or allergen exposure pattern, lack of fever.

why_considered: The reported symptoms can occur with several respiratory and systemic conditions.
additional_information_needed: Presence of breathing difficulty or chest tightness
Resting heart rate / pulse oxygen level if home pulse oximeter available
Any over-the-counter or prescription medications already taken
follow_up_questions: What is your exact body temperature when measured with a thermometer?
Are you experiencing any shortness of breath, wheezing, or difficulty catching your breath?
Have you noticed any chest tightness, stiff neck, or severe dizziness?
medical_attention: Seek professional medical evaluation if symptoms are severe, worsening or concerning.

triage.escalation_recommendation: Schedule a consultation with a healthcare provider if symptoms persist beyond 3-5 days or worsen.

disclaimer: This is an informational AI analysis and not a medical diagnosis.
